title: Landscape Social-Ecological-Technical Dependency Semantics
direction: A dependency edge means the dependent node requires its provider node.
dependency_groups: Every declared group is mandatory (AND across groups); within one group, any one operational provider alternative is sufficient (OR across alternatives).
support_rule: A node is operational only if it has not failed and every declared dependency group has at least one non-disabled edge to an operational provider.
cycles: Rejected in v0. Static prerequisite graphs must be acyclic; feedback loops require a separate dynamic model and are not approximated by this contract.
scenario_forcing: A scenario may fail named nodes and/or disable named dependency edges. These are injected structural stressors, not probabilities or physical predictions.
cause_reporting: Unsupported nodes report direct failed-node status or unsatisfied dependency groups, with each provider alternative marked operational, node-failed, edge-disabled, or dependency-unavailable so callers can trace upstream causes.
out_of_scope: No hydrology, canopy-growth, thermal-comfort, biodiversity, economic, legal, or causal model is run.
No failure probabilities, recovery time, feedback delay, or physical capacity is inferred.
No dependency edge is treated as observed fact unless an upstream application supplies and qualifies it.
